newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH GDANSK REFINERY JOINS FUEL PRICE RAISES.
newsitem.headline: POLISH GDANSK REFINERY JOINS FUEL PRICE RAISES.

text.p: Poland's second biggest oil refinery Rafineria Gdanska SA will raise petrol and diesel fuel prices on Friday night in line with a Wednesday finance ministry regulation, the refinery's spokeswoman said.

Ewa Sielicka said in a statement the refinery would raise its prices for retailers in a way which would result in retail prices of the 94-octane leaded and 95-octane unleaded petrol. rising no more than 0.01 zloty per litre.
The price of diesel fuel would increase to produce a retail price increase of no more than 0.06 zloty.

The ministry, which sets caps on fuel prices, raised the maximum diesel price by 4.9 percent to 1.28 zlotys per litre, and by 0.7 percent to 1.51 zlotys and 1.66 zlotys respectively for 94-octane leaded and 95-octane unleaded petrol.

The regulation is in force from October 9 until the end of the year. The ministry also cut the excise tax on imported and domestically produced diesel fuel by 60 zlotys per tonne to 400 zlotys and 360 zlotys respectively.
But Sielicka said the government moves would only partially improve the situation on the Polish fuel market.
"Both the price rise and the excise tax cut on diesel will only partially compensate costs of purchase of very expensive crude oil on world markets," Sielicka wrote in the statement.
The rise of world oil prices in recent months hard hit Polish importers and producers, who are bound by official caps on fuel prices.
The finance ministry was long reluctant to rise official ceilings fearing such a move be an inflationary impulse which would finally upset the official 17 percent inflation target for this year.
Earlier today Poland's biggest Plock refinery also announced it raised its prices by the amount allowed by the ministry as of October 11.
